system_prompt_style.evidence_quote:
You are a security engineer proficient in vulnerability research. You need
to analyze vulnerabilities in {{language}} code, generate an executable
PoC
system_prompt_style.note: Supervisor prompt uses {{language}} variable rendered per run; sub-agent sys_prompt uses format placeholder {name}.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: - **`detailed_trace`**: Mapping from function names to actual source code snippets for precise reasoning.
env_context_strategy.note: Context comes from injected white-box analysis reports (trace, call_chain, detailed_trace code snippets, class_constructors) rather than a file tree. Closest value is file_tree_summary, meaning context is injected up front; this does not fit the value list exactly, so the case belongs under Ambiguities. The toolkit (installJavaPackage, executeJavaCode, findSanitizer, etc.) has no generic view/grep tools, so agent_driven_navigation is not supported and mixed is not coded. A single value is given as a string because A2 is single-valued.

context_compaction.evidence_quote:
It splits the large alert
information into several shorter prompts, preventing each from ex-
ceeding the maximum token limit
context_compaction.note: No history_processor/condenser/truncation of conversation history found in the evidence; constraint accumulation splits prompts but does not shrink message history.

observation_format.evidence_quote:
For runtime information, the agent records the execution traces.
If there is a runtime error in PoC execution, it also records the error
stack.
observation_format.note: Observations are text (compilation/runtime error messages, execution traces).

tool_call_format.evidence_quote:
Respond with specific tags as outlined below:
<observation>{what you observe}</observation>
<thought>{what you thought}</thought>
<action>{the action name you want to call}</action>
tool_call_format.note: Actions selected via <action> tags parsed from text (AgentScope ReAct).

tool_count.evidence_quote:
service_toolkit.add(installJavaPackage)
        service_toolkit.add(initJavaEnvironment)
        service_toolkit.add(executeJavaCode)
        service_toolkit.add(generateJavaCode)
        service_toolkit.add(reflectSelfCritics)
        service_toolkit.add(findSanitizer)
        service_toolkit.add(final_output)
tool_count.note: JavaAgent registers 7 tools; JS agent registers 7 (installJsModule, executeJsCode, generateJsCode, findSanitizer, reflectSelfCritics, final_output, initJsEnvironment). Supervisor exposes sub-agents as actions (6 actions incl. Finish).

edit_primitive.note: Code generation produces complete exploit script code (lastScriptCode full file), not a diff or search/replace edit tool.

tool_schema_source.note: AgentScope ServiceToolkit derives function schemas from Python function signatures/docstrings via add().

protocol_standardization.note: Tools registered directly via ServiceToolkit; no MCP/A2A client in the VulnSage agent code shown; AgentScope service registry only.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote:
The Validation Agent and Reflec-
tion Agents form a feedback-driven self-refinement loop that uses
execution traces and runtime error analysis to either improve the
exploit iteratively
loop_primitives.note: Supervisor follows ReAct; validation executes exploit and reflection agents repair -> generate_test_repair.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote:
we do not explicitly enforce the super-
visor agent to follow a fixed order of taking actions
planning_granularity.note: Planning only in ReAct free-text reasoning; no stored plan object.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote:
One supervisor agent at the top accepts the library code as the
input, invokes sub-agents to discover exploitable vulnerabilities
multi_agent_topology.note: Supervisor Agent orchestrates specialized sub-agents (Code Analyzer, Code Generation, Validation, Reflection).

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote:
invokes sub-agents to discover exploitable vulnerabilities
with valid exploit code
delegation_mechanism.note: Supervisor invokes sub-agents as actions; work handed to distinct agent instances.

human_in_loop.evidence_quote:
the supervisor will pick one of
them after the Validation Agent responds
human_in_loop.note: Fully automated CLI run; no confirmation/approval gate found in evidence.

short_term_state.note: Agent state is message list in TemporaryMemory; constraints accumulated are passed in prompts.

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: In-memory memory module, not writing to hard disk
long_term_memory.note: No cross-run persisted memory/skills used by VulnSage agents in evidence.

state_persistence.evidence_quote:
If we let VulnSage restart from scratch, it may nevertheless eventually
produce a working exploit.
state_persistence.note: Runs restart from scratch; no resume of interrupted state found.

self_verification.evidence_quote:
The Validation Agent checks whether the exploit succeeds by exe-
cuting the code in a sandbox. If it fails, it provides runtime feedback
self_verification.note: Validation Agent runs the exploit (test_execution enforced by harness); Reflection/reflectSelfCritics provide self_critique. Also static/dynamic anti-cheat checks.

retry_policy.evidence_quote:
For each alert, VulnSage is allowed at most 20 attempts to
generate a valid result.
retry_policy.note: max_iters=25 (Java) / 20 (JS) per agent; up to 20 attempts per alert.

rollback.evidence_quote:
the Code Generation Agent then utilizes an LLM
to generate candidate exploits.
rollback.note: Exploits regenerated afresh each round; no undo/git-reset rollback of file changes found in evidence.

termination_condition.evidence_quote:
this feature lets the Supervisor Agent terminate it-
self when it calls the finish action once it generates the exploit or
concludes that the alert is a false positive.
termination_condition.note: Finish action = model_declared; max_iters (25/20) and 20 attempts per alert = max_steps.

cost_controls.evidence_quote:
each vulnerability costs
$0.97. In the worst-case scenario, the cost is $3.49.
cost_controls.note: Cost measured but no token_budget/routing/caching mechanism found in evidence.

timeouts.evidence_quote:
The Validation Agent prepares an
executable environment for exploits and verifies exploit validity
timeouts.note: No per-tool or per-run timeout found in the provided evidence.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: We assume you have Docker and Docker Compose installed.
execution_isolation.note: Frontend and validation server run in Docker containers; exploit executed in server sandbox.

filesystem_access.evidence_quote:
The Validation Agent checks whether the exploit succeeds by exe-
cuting the code in a sandbox.
filesystem_access.note: Code executed in sandbox container with package install; full access within container boundary.

network_policy.evidence_quote: JNDI Injection: The execution requests an evil JNDI provider.
network_policy.note: Exploits make network requests (JNDI/LDAP); no egress restriction found.

permission_model.evidence_quote:
the Validation Agent performs
an analysis and rejects it if it contains direct command-execution
API calls (like Runtime.exec, child\_process.exec).
permission_model.note: Anti-cheat blocklist of direct command-execution APIs; closest to static_allowlist (blocklist).

tracing.evidence_quote: For runtime information, the agent records the execution traces.
tracing.note: Execution info (compilation + runtime traces) recorded; AgentScope studio logging available. Closest to structured_traces.

replayability.evidence_quote:
If we let VulnSage restart from scratch, it may nevertheless eventually
produce a working exploit.
replayability.note: No replay/resume mechanism for recorded trajectories found in evidence.

eval_hooks.evidence_quote: server/ — Source code of the validation environment (Go).
eval_hooks.note: Validation server evaluates whether exploits succeed against oracles; ships in repo (server/).

guardrails.evidence_quote:
the validation
pipeline applies both static and dynamic anti-cheat checks.
guardrails.note: Anti-cheat static/dynamic checks reject exploits calling command-execution APIs directly -> action_policies.

target_domain.evidence_quote:
we propose VulnSage, a multi-
agent framework for AEG.
target_domain.note: Automated exploit generation / software vulnerability domain; coded swe + other (security/AEG).

open_source.evidence_quote: The internal white-box analysis engine is not open-sourced due to licensing restrictions.
open_source.note: Frontend and server open-sourced; static analysis engine closed.

model_agnostic.evidence_quote:
we replace our default LLM (Qwen3-Max) with
others to study how the LLM affects our approach.
model_agnostic.note: AgentScope supports multiple providers (openai, anthropic, dashscope, litellm, etc.); evaluated GPT-4o, DeepSeek, Qwen.

primary_artifact.evidence_quote:
We open-sourced our implementation anonymously in https:
//github.com/Vulnsage/VulnSage.
primary_artifact.note: Pinned to repo commit; paper ICPC 2026.

first_release_date.note: No tags in evidence; using pinned commit date as basis.

pinned_version.note: No release tag; pinned to main commit.
